trust_decision.summary: Whether a local MCP server container is network-isolated (and therefore whether the egress proxy that denies host.docker.internal exists at all) is decided by two defaulting sites: the default value of the --isolate-network CLI flag and the default value of the network_isolation field on the API workload request; the decision is consumed at docker DeployWorkload, which only creates the internal network, DNS and egress squid containers when isolateNetwork is true.

landing_point.why: The summary names host.docker.internal, so an engineer looks first at the deny rules that block the Docker gateway hostnames; those rules already exist and only run inside the egress proxy, so the real defect (the proxy is not created unless the user opts in) sits two layers away in the flag/request defaults.

fix_sites.entry_point: networkIsolationEnabled helper used by the two HTTP workload entry points

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Kubernetes runtime's DeployWorkload accepts the isolateNetwork argument as `_ bool` and discards it, and the package's permission-profile parameter is already `_ *permissions.Profile` with a TODO; a solver can argue host.docker.internal and the Docker gateway are Docker-only, that pod egress needs a NetworkPolicy feature, and that the Kubernetes path was never part of this Docker-default advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Servers that legitimately need direct host or internet access must keep working through the two documented opt-outs: --isolate-network=false and --allow-docker-gateway. An over-broad fix (forcing isolation regardless of the flag, or dropping the gateway opt-in) breaks them; the published fix itself had to add --isolate-network=false to six existing e2e call sites for the osv, proxy-stdio and vmcp yardstick servers.

O6_input_shapes: CLI flag omitted (thv run with no --isolate-network) -> defaults to true
API JSON network_isolation absent (nil pointer) -> true
API response now always serializes the field so an explicit false survives a GET->edit round trip

O8_uncovered_routes.route: thv run --from-config <file>: the exported RunConfig JSON is replayed through runner.ReadJSON and deployed as-is; isolate_network is a plain bool with omitempty, so an absent key means no isolation and nothing applies the new default
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Import replays a config the user exported or reviewed verbatim; the JSON contract preserves what the file says, so treating a missing key as off looks like intended behaviour rather than the same policy gap
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: cmd/thv/app and pkg/runner, 2 packages from the deny rules and separate from the two fixed defaulting sites

O8_uncovered_routes.route: thv tui dashboard launch: buildRunConfigFromRegistry builds the RunConfig in-process with runner.WithName/WithImage/WithTransportAndPorts/... and never calls WithNetworkIsolation, so a server started from the dashboard has isolate_network=false and is deployed with no egress proxy
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The TUI is an interactive convenience wrapper around the same run; its run form has no isolation control, so the omission reads as a UI gap and not as the documented thv run default
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/tui, a separate package from cmd/thv/app and pkg/api/v1

O8_uncovered_routes.route: thv inspector deploys the inspector UI container through rt.DeployWorkload with isolateNetwork hard-coded false
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Auxiliary ToolHive-owned container (MCP Inspector UI), not a user MCP server, and it must reach the local proxy port on the host
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: cmd/thv/app, same package as the fixed CLI flag but a different deploy call site; 2 packages from the sink's defaulting layer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: vMCP embedding service deploys the TEI model container through rt.DeployWorkload with isolateNetwork hard-coded false
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Auxiliary inference container with a required 127.0.0.1 port binding and a host bind-mounted model cache, not an MCP server
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/vmcp/cli, 3 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make RunConfig.IsolateNetwork a *bool and default it in ReadJSON/LoadState so every import and reload path inherits the new default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RunConfig is declared part of the API contract and is the single choke point for export/import and saved state; a maintainer fixing 'isolation must default on' would naturally put the default where every consumer passes through

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add runner.WithNetworkIsolation(true) to the TUI builder option list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The TUI builds the same RunConfig in-process as thv run with a parallel option list, so the missing option is exactly the kind of copy a maintainer would add late

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Re-derive the isolation default when rebuilding an old RunConfig during workload upgrade
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The upgrade applier already re-picks every other setting from the old config; a 'default isolation on upgrade' sibling fits the existing pattern of preserve-and-warn

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Honour isolateNetwork in the Kubernetes runtime (default-deny egress NetworkPolicy per workload)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Deployer interface already carries the argument, so a maintainer closing the same hole for the cluster runtime would implement it here

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Isolate auxiliary containers (inspector UI, TEI embedding) or gate them behind an explicit opt-out
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both auxiliary containers deploy through the same DeployWorkload primitive, so a default-on policy invites a matching change at those call sites

O9_family: Improper access control / insecure default: local MCP server containers are not network-isolated by default, so they can reach host services on the Docker gateway (CWE-284, CWE-306)

services: Docker daemon for e2e and any real deploy
no external service needed for the unit-level decision tests
